items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: the singers would come in like Edie and whatever her husband’s name

ctx.x: I was sorry to hear that you lost some instruments.

I lost a lot of good instruments man. See I used to be — another part of my life too, I played a lot of shows, see all the Broadway shows that came to New Orleans and big band things when the singers would come in like Edie and whatever her husband’s name

and Ella Fitzgerald and Gladys Knight, the Four Tops or whoever it was, I was, I do a lot of contracting and I got a friend of mine who used to say I get all the black acts, he’d get all the white acts. And we are very close friends now, I mean we talk all the time. So the hotels and stuff isn’t running no more, and I used to play the Fairmont with him in the Blue Room and the acts would come through, and sometimes I’d be on the show if they needed five saxophones I’d always be in there somewhere, four, five and…
